upcoming.expectation: USDA's fourth survey-based corn and soybean yields of the season, and the first to fold in October's harvest results. The trade looks for corn to come down from 178.5 to 177.8 bu/acre (range 173.2 to 182.1) and soybeans to edge up from 52.8 to 52.9 (range 51.4 to 54.1) (Reuters survey, via Pro Farmer, 2026-10). The range bar below is the corn yield survey only.

history.reaction: Corn stocks printed 2.095 billion bushels, above the entire pre-report trade range (1.843–2.005B), not just the 1.918B average. A real miss: more old-crop corn was sitting in bins and elevators on September 1 than any surveyed analyst had guessed.

Soybean stocks printed 0.315 billion bushels, under the 0.324B trade average and inside the survey's 0.304–0.349B range. Below average, but some analyst on record expected this level, so it is not graded a surprise.

Wheat stocks printed 1.846 billion bushels. No trade estimate was on file to grade this against, the only survey found had a wheat figure that didn't reconcile against a cited WASDE number, so it was withheld rather than published. The print stands on the record; it just isn't scored.

USDA put 2026/27 corn carryout at 1.567 billion bushels, 34M above the 1.533B trade average (Dow Jones survey, via DTN). No survey low or high is on file for this figure, so it is graded on the 2% band.

USDA put 2026/27 soybean carryout at 310M, 20M above the 290M trade average (Dow Jones survey, via DTN). Reuters' survey averaged 298M; the print was above that too. No survey low or high is on file for this figure, so it is graded on the 2% band.

USDA's first survey-based corn yield came in at 180.7, 2.3 under July and 1.3 under the trade's 182.0. More acres (planted up 1.4M to 96.7M) kept production near-record at 16.013B bu, but the market traded the yield cut and the 1.653B carryout (down from 1.79B): December corn settled up 15 cents at $4.78.

Soybean yield printed 52.7, a couple tenths under both July and the trade, effectively in line. The acreage add (planted up 1.4M to 86.8M) still makes 4.519B bu the largest soybean crop on record, and carryout ticked up to 320M. November beans settled up 12 cents at $11.84, riding corn's coattails more than their own numbers.

New-crop wheat carryout came in at 744M, 21M under the 765M trade average and 18M under May, but inside the survey's 740–804M range, so some analyst on record expected this level. The cut came from a smaller Hard Red Winter crop (all-wheat production trimmed to 1,543M, yield 47.0); the season-average farm price was cut $0.50 to $6.00.
